Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS : 6992 - 1982 

3. Materials 

3.1 Timber — Furniture class as given in 13:399-1963 'Classification of commercial timbers and 
their zonal distribution (rev/sec/)' shall be used. The timber shall be seasoned as given in 
IS: 287-1973 'Recommendations for maximum permissible moisture content of timber used for 
different purposes (second revision)'. The hardwood of any species may be used provided the 
timber is given suitable preservative treatment [ see IS : 401-1967 Code of practice for preservation 
of timber ( second revision ) ]. 

3.2 Joints — Conforming to relevant details given in IS : 3845-1966 * Code of practice for joints used 
m wooden furniture \ 

3.3 Seat and Back — Either with a cane insert or upholstered. Solid seat with a foam rubber 
cushion shall be supplied if specially asked for by the purchaser. ,i 

3.4 Legrest and Footrest — Upholstered. 

3.5 Castors— Normal duty swiveHing castors, conforming to designation HN 75 of IS: 4034-1979 
1 Specification for castors for hospital equipment {first revision) \ 

3.6 Hinges — Continuous ( piano ) hinges conforming to Type 1 of IS : 3818-1971 ' Specification for 
continuous ( piano ) hinges (first revision) ' or butt hinges conforming to size 100 B of IS : 205-1978 
1 Specification for non-ferrous metal butt hinges ( third revision ) \ 

3.7 Other components — Suitable material intended for the purpose. 

4. Requirements 

4.1 The back shall be capable of tilting between 80° and 120 Q to the seat. The tilting shall be 
achieved by a grooved bracket. The bracket shall be capable of being clamped in position to 
prevent it from accidentally falling backwards when the patient rests against the back. Tilting ^hall 
only apply to the back. 

4.2 The legrest shall be capable of being fixed at different angles between 0°and 90° to the vertical. 
The clamping of legrest at these angles shall be positive and shall not loosen accidentally or under 
load. 

4.3 The distance of footrest to seat shall be adjustable to suit the leg length of the user. The 
locking arrangement for adjustments shall be positive and the footrest length shall not change 
unless intended. 

4.4 The various hinges used in the chair shall be sturdy and shall be rigidly fixed. 

4.5 The adjusting mechanisms shall be sturdy and shall be easy to operate. The adjustments shall 
be capable of being carried out smoothly without undue effort. 

4.6 Provision shall be made in the seat to fit a partition to keep the knees of the patient apart. 

4.7 When the chair is placed on a level surface it shall not rock and shall be completely stable. 

4.8 A tray laminated with thermosetting synthetic resin bonded sheets [see IS: 2046-1969 
Specification for decorativethermosetting synthetic resin bonded laminated sheets (first revision)]. 
for keeping toys and other items shall be fixed on the armrest. This tray shall be removable when 
not required. 

4.9 All edges likely to be touched by the patiervt shall be rounded and shall be nowhere sharp. All 
surfaces coming into contact with the body of the patient shall be smooth and free from sharp 
imperfections likely to injure the patient. 

4.10 The chair shall be polished either with wax polish or transparent greasy French polish (see 
IS -.348-1958 Specification for French polish ). 

4.11 The web straps each at the armrest and backrest shall be provided with the chair. 

5. Tests 

5.0 The chair without castors shall be tested as described in 5.1. 

5.1 Dropping Test— As in 5.1.4 of IS : 5416-1969 'Methods of test for general purpose wooden 

chairs \ 



iS : 6992 - 1982 

5.2 When the chair with castors is pushed over a level and even surface without any load, it shall 
not wobble or rattle. It shall also move freely when pulled in circular motion and the castors shall 
align in the same direction without offering any resistance. 

6. Marking — Each chair shall have a label affixed to it giving the manufacturer's name, initials or 
recognized trade-mark. 

6.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

7. Packing — As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard has been revised keeping in view the advancement in technology and latest 
development in the manufacture of the chair. 

In this standard the major changes are for the provision of the two straps each at the 
armrest and backrest and use of laminated tray. The size of castors has also been specified. 



Printed at Arcee Press, New Delhi, India
